visual.general_description: Colored schematic diagram of the PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4/B7 immune checkpoint interactions between a T cell, a tumor cell and an antigen-presenting cell, with antibody icons for anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 and anti-CTLA-4.
visual.detailed_description: Cartoon on a white background. A large light-blue circle at upper left, labeled "T cell", contains a darker purple nucleus. From its right edge two parallel yellow stalks end in yellow receptor heads labeled "PD-1"; these face two red oval ligand heads labeled "PD-L1" on dark-red stalks extending to a pink irregular cell at right labeled "Tumor cell" (darker pink nucleus, small dots). From the lower edge of the T cell two dark purple stalks end in a pair of dark purple lobes labeled "CTLA-4", which sit against a pair of orange oval units labeled "B7"; the orange units connect by brown stalks to a lavender irregular cell at bottom labeled "APC" (darker nucleus, small light spots). Three Y-shaped antibody icons with colored labels are present: purple "anti-PD-1 antibodies" at top near the T cell side of the PD-1/PD-L1 junction, light-blue "anti-PD-L1 antibodies" at top right above the PD-L1 side, and green "anti-CTLA-4 antibodies" at left beside the CTLA-4/B7 pair. There are no arrows, numeric values, scale bars, panel letters, patient features, identifiers or imaging data.

evidence.quote: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) emerged as a novel therapy in oncology

mentioned_categories.as_documented: PD-L1 expressed by tumor cells binds to PD-1 on activated T cells

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Mechanisms of action of the main ICl agents currently in use. PD-L1 expressed by tumor cells binds to PD-1 on activated T cells, inhibiting cytotoxic T cell activity. B7 expressed by APCs acts as a co-inhibitory signal through CTLA-4 located on T cells. Blocking either CTLA-4 or PD-1/PD-L1 using specific antibodies results in T cell activation and cytotoxic antitumoral effect.
